gridLegend.A: BoardPlate (stand on and ACTIVE to open linked BoardDoor)
gridLegend.D: BoardDoor (blocking until linked BoardPlate is activated)
gridLegend.0-9: BoardPortal paired endpoints (reserved in schema; not placed in this validated pack)

coordinateSystem: x increases right, y increases down, zero indexed

commandRules.REPETE: infinite loop, no repeat count; stop on victory/failure/user stop/safety halt
commandRules.SI: if condition true evaluate child instructions; conditions are free logical tests
commandRules.actionCount: every executed primitive command costs one; SI/REPETE control nodes cost zero
commandRules.UTILISE: while facing locked door and holding key; opens door and consumes key
commandRules.ACTIVE: standing on switch, opens gate permanently
commandRules.POUSSE: crate immediately in front is moved one cell forward; robot occupies former crate location
commandRules.finishWithKeyWorld3: flag only counts if holding collectible key; no UTILISE needed
commandRules.inventory: Integer key count; each RAMASSE adds one; each UTILISE on a distinct locked cell consumes one. No one-key-only assumption.
commandRules.pairedDoors: BoardDoor is never decorative or optional: it blocks a mandatory passage and remains closed until the paired BoardPlate is activated using ACTIVE. linkId defines one-to-one active link for this pack.
commandRules.multipleCrates: All BoardCrate states tracked as independent positions. A push moves only the crate immediately ahead.

generationPolicy.cumulativeMechanics: From World 4 onward, later levels require multiple keys/locks. Worlds5-10 introduce multiple crates, plates and doors with cumulative interactions.
generationPolicy.pathAlgorithm: Random DFS perfect maze on 4x4 logical nodes expanded to 7x7; 7x7 maze contains dead ends and nontrivial corridor turns.
generationPolicy.worlds7to10: REPETE performs at least two AVANCE primitive actions before victory. Worlds8-10 SI condition evaluated both true and false.
generationPolicy.validation: 100 solutions replayed in deterministic simulator. Additional structural BFS proof for every door: if the door is sealed while other interactive objects are considered passable, the finish is unreachable. Does not prove that the solution is optimal.
generationPolicy.multipleInstances: Advanced worlds can contain multiple BoardKey, BoardLock, BoardCrate, BoardPlate and BoardDoor; up to 3 pairs of buttons and doors in the most complex levels. Every door is required rather than decorative.
generationPolicy.gateUsage: BoardDoor only at mandatory corridor bottlenecks, never as a decorative or bypassable obstacle. Unneeded gate objects removed or relocated; occasionally extra existing blocking tiles form real corridors.

assetPolicy: Only the 15 supplied Board* assets. Robot is an independent sprite overlay, not a tile asset.

tileStacking.base: BoardGrass under every walkable object/start/goal, and BoardGrass as entire empty surface
tileStacking.object: BoardFlag, BoardKey, BoardLock, BoardPlate, BoardDoor, BoardCrate, BoardPortal or robot overlay

portals.reason: No teleportation rule or paired-portal solution existed in the validated source levels; adding them without regenerating and solving would invalidate validation.
portals.futureRule: paired id / linked coordinates, teleport on entry, avoid immediate bounce, validate routes with updated engine

interactionRules.BoardKey: Multiple BoardKey possible; each collected with RAMASSE on its cell; inventory increments by 1.
interactionRules.BoardLock: Multiple BoardLock possible; each UTILISE opens only the lock facing robot, consuming one key.
interactionRules.BoardPlate: Multiple buttons possible; ACTIVE on the current plate activates its linkId and opens only linked doors (persists).
interactionRules.BoardDoor: Only placed in a mandatory passage. Blocks traversal until linked BoardPlate is activated using ACTIVE. Every door has a matching linkId and is required to reach the finish.
interactionRules.BoardCrate: Several boxes may coexist and move independently; POUSSE moves only the one directly ahead into the next free cell.
interactionRules.BoardFlag: arrive at flag; World 3 also requires holding key
interactionRules.BoardPortal: Reserved; portals not used; no teleportation rules currently established.

validationScope: V6: 100/100 simulated programs reach flag; BoardDoor mandatory bottleneck independently checked by graph reachability; every door has a linked BoardPlate and a preceding ACTIVE command. No claim of optimality.

migrationFromV3.breakingChanges: Entire level grids, mechanics and provided programs redesigned; top-level JSON and most level keys retained

multiObjectPolicy.keys: BoardKey instances are indistinguishable and stack in integer inventory; more than one key can be picked.
multiObjectPolicy.locks: Each BoardLock opens independently; one key consumed per UTILISE; when opened its terrain is passable.
multiObjectPolicy.crates: BoardCrate positions in a set or object list; each has its own collision and mutable position.
multiObjectPolicy.platesAndDoors: Each BoardDoor belongs to a BoardPlate with the same linkId. Every door occupies an essential articulation cell: without opening that one door, reaching the flag is impossible even if all other interactive obstacles are considered passable.
multiObjectPolicy.serialization: Each object retains type,x,y; plates and doors require linkId for levels with multiple.
multiObjectPolicy.walkableGround: BoardGrass underneath every object except blocking terrain; objects drawn above ground.

migrationFromV4.kept: level ids, 7x7 coordinates, existing assets, first two worlds and progression
migrationFromV4.new: additional instances, independent switch/door linkId, key count inventory and revised programs, validated against simulator
requiresCodeChange: keys as count rather than boolean
crates and locks as collections rather than optional single instance

migrationFromV5.kept: 100 level IDs, 7x7 size, previous mechanic and command definitions
migrationFromV5.changes: doors relocated to mandatory corridors and bypasses closed with blocking tiles, occasional gate pairs removed; RI-075 replaced by mirrored alternate puzzle because existing path had no mandatory gate position

doorPlacementPolicy.meaning: Only use BoardDoor when crossing that cell is necessary to reach BoardFlag.
doorPlacementPolicy.activation: Must have one BoardPlate with same linkId, activated by ACTIVE before crossing BoardDoor.
doorPlacementPolicy.validation: Static geometric reachability: remove only this door from accessible terrain; even if all other interactive entities are treated as passable, the finish must remain unreachable.
doorPlacementPolicy.forbidden: Do not put doors off the player route, decoratively, or where an alternate walkable bypass avoids the door.
